title: Constructible exceptional adjunction and its coefficient comparisons without an ambient datum
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and the finite discrete rings $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; $X,Y$ are not required to be separated over $k$. For $\Lambda\in\{A_n,R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ use ordinary constant-$A_n$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites at finite levels, completed coefficient sheaves and derived-complete constructible objects at $R$, raw scalar localization at $E$, and common finite coefficient-field stages at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ for the full bounded constructible finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use compact supports $F_\Lambda=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and the constructible exceptional functor $G_\Lambda=Rf^!_\Lambda$ constructed by etale comparison and strict coefficient systems [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The functors $F_\Lambda$ and $G_\Lambda$ preserve these finite-Tor categories and are exact, and there is an adjunction
$$F_\Lambda:\mathcal C_{X,\Lambda}\rightleftarrows\mathcal C_{Y,\Lambda}:G_\Lambda,\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_Y(F_\Lambda K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,G_\Lambda L),$$
natural in $K,L$. Its units $\eta_\Lambda$ and counits $\epsilon_\Lambda$ obey both triangle identities and the compactification-refinement comparisons.

For every finite extension $E\subset E'$ put $R'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi'$ of $R'$, and put $A_{E',r}=R'/(\varpi'^r)$ for $r\ge1$; the notation $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda'}$, $F_{\Lambda'}$ and $G_{\Lambda'}$ at these target coefficient stages uses the same constructions with $E'$ in place of $E$. Finite coefficient change means derived extension of scalars along the displayed map of constant ring sheaves, integral reduction is [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], integral scalar extension is [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and rational scalar extension and rationalization are [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

For each coefficient change $T_T:\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}\to\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda'}$ given by a finite quotient $A_n\to A_m$ ($1\le m\le n$), integral reduction $R\to A_n$, finite-level scalar extension $A_n\to B_n=\mathcal O_{E'}/\varpi^n\mathcal O_{E'}$ for a finite extension $E\subset E'$ and any further coefficient quotient, integral or rational scalar extension along such an extension, or rationalization $R\to E$, the canonical comparisons
$$q:T_YF_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}T_X,\qquad b:T_XG_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\Lambda'}T_Y$$
are isomorphisms on the stated domains and satisfy, with the components evaluated at the indicated objects,
$$G_{\Lambda'}(q_K)\circ b_{F_\Lambda K}\circ T_X(\eta_{\Lambda,K})=\eta_{\Lambda',T_XK},$$
$$\epsilon_{\Lambda',T_YL}\circ F_{\Lambda'}(b_L)\circ q_{G_\Lambda L}=T_Y(\epsilon_{\Lambda,L}).$$
For the finite-level scalar change, if $e=e(E'/E)$ and $\varpi'$ is a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_{E'}$, then $(\varpi^n)=(\varpi'^{en})$, so $B_n$ is the coefficient ring $A_{E',en}$; any further quotient is to $A_{E',m}$ with $1\le m\le en$. These comparisons satisfy the identity and composition cocycles, commute with shifts, and define the corresponding comparisons in the common-stage category. For field coefficients finite reduction refers to chosen integral representatives before rationalization, not to a reduction functor on the field category. No right adjoint on an unrestricted pro-etale ambient category is asserted.

source.place: Paragraphs defining the constructible exceptional functor, its higher coefficient stages and the natural adjunction isomorphisms; theorem obligations explicitly distinguished from the optional ambient datum.

proof.text: Work first at a fixed finite coefficient stage and a fixed compactification (c=(j,p_f)). The scheme (overline X) is finite type over (k): finite affine covers of (Y) and of the finite-type morphism (p_f) give finitely generated coordinate algebras over (k). Choose a nonnegative dimension bound (d) by lem-kun-dimension-finite-type (take (d=0) for the empty scheme). The open-extension theorem puts (j_!K) in the finite-Tor category with its original interval ([a,b]); cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale gives (F_AK=Rp_{f,*}j_!K) constructible with interval ([a,b+2d]). Finite type over the Noetherian field makes all schemes Noetherian. Open extension and proper derived direct image are exact by the two triangulated-functor nodes, so (F_A) is exact on the finite-Tor subcategory and its compactification refinements agree.

source.place: Construction 2.17, Theorem 2.18 and Corollary 2.19; finite-stage compact supports and amplitude bounds.

proof.text: Work on the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories. The compactification has Noetherian source and target by Step 1, so thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint supplies $F_A^{\mathrm{et}}=Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j_!^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv G_A^{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class to the same compactification: for bounded-below pro-etale $L$ it gives the bounded-below composite $G_AL=\nu_X^*G_A^{\mathrm{et}}R\nu_{Y,*}L$ and its natural Hom bijection for bounded-below etale-origin inputs. This is exactly the finite functor defined in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image. The preservation corollary applies to this specified composite, including nonseparated finite-type $X,Y$, and gives constructibility and finite-Tor bounds. Thus the Hom bijection restricts to the full finite-Tor constructible categories. Its transpose formulas give units, counits and triangles. The unique adjoint shift comparison supplies coherent shifts and unit/counit compatibility; the triangulated-right-adjoint lemma then gives exactness. No Brown theorem is applied to a pro-etale category or to an unspecified localizing closure.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29(2), 3.16(2), with the current blueprint exceptional-functor paragraph.

proof.text: A finite-Tor input has a bounded flat model by lem-sf-flat-model. After extension from (A) to a finite coefficient ring (B), tensoring with a (B)-module is the original flat tensor followed by restriction, so the same Tor interval is retained; no flatness of a quotient (A_n\to A_m) is used. The finite-tensor constructibility theorem gives constructible cohomology, and refining the finite etale trivializing covers makes the induced (B)-action locally constant with finite (B)-stalks. K-flat change of rings is independent of the chosen model by lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings. Hence all finite coefficient-change functors in the statement have the displayed domains; higher stages are handled below.

source.place: Finite-coefficient tensor and change-of-rings argument in the coefficient-comparison part of the construction.

proof.text: On ordinary etale categories use $F_A^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv G_A^{\mathrm{et}}$. Exact restriction of scalars $r_T$ is conservative. Open extension commutes with restriction termwise, and ringed-topos direct-image composition gives $r_YF_B^{\mathrm{et}}\cong F_A^{\mathrm{et}}r_X$. Derived scalar extension $T_T$ is left adjoint to $r_T$, computed by K-flat models. Define $q:T_YF_A^{\mathrm{et}}\to F_B^{\mathrm{et}}T_X$ by transposing $F_A^{\mathrm{et}}$ of the scalar unit. After restriction it is the constant-$B$ projection map of lem-pur-etale-exceptional-constant-tensor, hence an isomorphism. The Hom chain using $T\dashv r$, $F_A\dashv G_A$, $F_B\dashv G_B$ and $q$ identifies $r_XG_B^{\mathrm{et}}\cong G_A^{\mathrm{et}}r_Y$. Under this identification, restriction of the counit-transpose map $b:T_XG_A^{\mathrm{et}}\to G_B^{\mathrm{et}}T_Y$ is precisely the constant-$B$ exceptional tensor map of that same lemma: both have transpose the inverse projection map followed by $1\otimes\epsilon_A$. That lemma makes it invertible even when $B$ is nonflat over $A$; conservativity then proves that $b$ is invertible as a $B$-linear map. The identity and composite $q$ comparisons are the tensor associators on K-flat models.

source.place: Ordinary etale coefficient comparison and exceptional adjunction.

proof.text: Transport the preceding comparison across the etale--pro-etale constructible-origin equivalence. The Tor-amplitude comparison preserves the same interval, the site-comparison unit identifies (R\nu_*\nu^*) with the identity on bounded-below etale complexes, and the compact-support comparison identifies pro-etale (F_A) with the transported etale (F_A^{\mathrm{et}}). Exact inverse image commutes with tensoring by a constant coefficient ring on a flat model, so the transported (q) is the canonical pro-etale coefficient map. The transported (b), units, and counits are the same maps because they are characterized by the natural Hom transposes; hence they are independent of witnesses and compactification choices.

proof.text:
For a coefficient map $T$, define $b_L:T_XG_AL\to G_BT_YL$ as the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_Y\epsilon_L\circ q_{G_AL}^{-1}$. The inverse-transpose formula gives the displayed counit equation. Put $a_K=b_{F_AK}\circ T_X\eta_{A,K}:T_XK\to G_BT_YF_AK$. Its inverse transpose is
$$T_Y\epsilon_{A,F_AK}\circ q_{G_AF_AK}^{-1}\circ F_BT_X\eta_{A,K}
=T_Y(\epsilon_{A,F_AK}\circ F_A\eta_{A,K})\circ q_K^{-1}=q_K^{-1},$$
by naturality of $q$ and the triangle identity. After postcomposing $a_K$ with $G_B(q_K)$, its inverse transpose is $q_K\circ q_K^{-1}=1_{F_BT_XK}$. This is also the inverse transpose of $\eta_{B,T_XK}$. Injectivity proves exactly the completed unit equation in the statement. The unique-adjoint coefficient lemma transports this counit-normalized comparison to any other adjoint choices; mate pasting applied to the identity and tensor-composition comparisons for $q$ proves the identity and composition cocycles for $b$.

Form $\mathsf S_A(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ with $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ (not an $\ell$-power reindexing). Apply lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint directly to the fixed compactification. It supplies an actual $R$-linear exact adjunction $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{et}}=Rp_{A,*}j_{!,A}\dashv\mathcal G^{\mathrm{et}}$ on ordinary unbounded etale system derived categories. In particular its stated canonical isomorphism $e_n\mathcal G^{\mathrm{et}}\cong G_{A_n}^{\mathrm{et}}e_n$ preserves evaluated units, counits and transition mates; its uniform lower bound and bounded-below normalization assertions apply here. These are conclusions of this cited theorem, not consequences asserted from $e_n\mathcal F^{\mathrm{et}}\cong F_{A_n}^{\mathrm{et}}e_n$ alone. Zheng Lemma 5.22 uses the derived evaluation-left-adjoint comparisons of Lemma 5.13 and (5.16.2). We use its system theorem, including that evaluation result, rather than constructing a different Brown adjoint and identifying it by evaluations. No separatedness of the structure maps of $X,Y$ is required by this theorem.

proof.text:
Write $C_T=\nu_{T,A}^*$ and $V_T=R\nu_{T,A,*}$ on actual derived systems. The system-comparison theorem and finite site-comparison unit make $C_T,V_T$ inverse equivalences between bounded-below etale systems and bounded-below pro-etale systems with etale-origin levels. Indeed the unit evaluates to the finite unit and is invertible by joint conservativity; the counit and preservation of normalization are stated by the system-comparison theorem. Form the compact-support system comparison $C_Y\mathcal F^{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal F^{\mathrm{proet}}C_X$: use the proper direct-image mate of the commuting inverse images, followed by the open comparison. These are actual system maps by derived system adjunction and direct-image composition. Their evaluations are the canonical finite comparisons, invertible by the finite proper and open comparison nodes; joint conservativity proves invertibility of the system comparison, without assuming faithfulness on maps. Consequently, for normalized bounded-below systems $M,N$ with constructible finite-Tor levels,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{proet}}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{et}}V_XM,V_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V_XM,\mathcal G^{\mathrm{et}}V_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,C_X\mathcal G^{\mathrm{et}}V_YN).$$
Thus the transported right functor is $\mathcal G=C_X\mathcal G^{\mathrm{et}}V_Y$, with actual system units, counits and triangles. Its transitions are the finite mates from Step 6 and Step 7, and it preserves normalization and common bounds. The composite $\mathcal G\mathcal R_Y$ is exactly $\mathcal T_f$ in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, before applying the derived limit.

proof.text: Use the ordinary reduction--limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$ on strict towers. Its unit is the map $P\to\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_TP$ whose compatible finite projections on one flat-term K-flat representative are the actual reduction maps $P\to\operatorname{Res}_n(P\otimes^L A_n)$; the total-limit cone is the stated (R\lim) cone, so for a derived-complete integral object the unit is an isomorphism by the (E'=E) case of the finite-free completed-scalar comparison. Its counit is an isomorphism on normalized towers by normalized-DVR effectivity. Hence derived-complete integral finite-Tor objects are equivalent to normalized towers with the common bounds required in the statement, and all maps are maps in the ordinary derived categories.

The common bounds required for the equivalence are uniform: Step 1 gives ([a,b+2d]) at every finite level for compact supports, and the admissibility theorem gives coefficient-independent bounds for the right adjoints. The integral compact-support comparison identifies the total limit and each finite reduction with (Rf_!K), while normalized effectivity identifies the right-adjoint tower with the completed (G_R). The integral finite-Tor category is triangulated, so the adjunction, units, counits and exactness descend from the tower category. For the exact integral finite-Tor predicate used by the coefficient system, prove triangulation directly: each scalarReductionDerivedExtension has its recorded triangulated and shift structures; the finite-stage tensor functor sends zero to zero, giving the common interval [0,0]; Tor amplitude transports along isomorphisms; the finite-stage shift clause gives [a-m,b-m] at every level; and the finite-stage extension clause gives [min(a,c),max(b,d)] uniformly. Intersect this uniform Tor property with the isomorphism-closed triangulated sfIntegralConstructible predicate. This is the Lean theorem ConstructibleExceptionalCoefficients.integralTriangulated and requires no finite-field datum or residue-field invertibility hypothesis.

source.place: Integral coefficient reconstruction and uniform bounds.

proof.text: For a finite extension (E\subset E'), the finite-free coefficient-system comparison transports the tower adjunction and its (q,b) maps. The subsequence (R'/\varpi^nR'=R'/\varpi'^{en}R') is cofinal; normalized transition maps recover every level (m) from any level (en\ge m), and the cocycle makes the result independent of the choice. The completed comparison (chi_{E'/E}) identifies this tower scalar extension with ordinary derived scalar extension and the integral scalar-extension definition; constructibility is preserved by the integral scalar-extension theorem.

source.place: Finite extension and ramification-index coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Localize the integral (R)-linear adjunction at (\varpi). Every integral constructible object has finite-Tor reductions by the residue-Tor theorem, so the preceding construction applies to every integral representative. The Hom bijections are (R)-linear, hence localization gives inverse natural Hom bijections for (E)-coefficients; units, counits, triangles, and coefficient cocycles are images of the integral ones. Finally represent two \(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\)-objects over a common finite coefficient field. Step 6 makes the finite-stage Hom bijections commute with every further scalar extension, so they pass to the directed colimit defining the common-stage category. This yields the adjunction and all comparisons for (E) and \(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\), with field reduction interpreted through an integral representative.

source.place: Rational localization and common finite coefficient stages.

proof.text: For a compactification refinement, transpose its compact-support comparison (a:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2) to obtain (\rho:G_2\to G_1). The counit equation is the inverse-transpose identity, and the unit equation follows by taking the two inverse transposes and using the triangle identity; mate pasting gives identity and composition. The shift comparison for the right adjoint is uniquely determined by the shift comparison for (F) and unit compatibility, and the shift-compatible natural transformations remain compatible under composition and whiskering. Therefore the adjunction, coefficient comparisons, refinement cocycles and shifts all satisfy the displayed identities. Empty schemes give zero functors and the stated zero bounds; ramified extensions use (en).
